policy: candidates: proved rules whose replacement is cheaper than the source; a rule that moves an operation to a wider type only if that type is not wider than the registers of the target

one_use_variant_selected: the rule has a variant that applies only if no interior value of the source has another user; where the rule fires and the variant does not, it removes no instruction (or it adds instructions), so the variant is used
plain_variant_selected: the variant of a rule that removes instructions also from a source with a shared interior value (with --no-regressions: and makes no file worse there)
variant_not_measured: one-use variants are selected by measurement only
not_emittable: the replacement cannot be written as an apply pattern
measured_regression: more instructions with the rule than without, with every candidate enabled or inside the selected set
worse_than_existing: alone, loses to the existing combiner on its own example
covered_by_existing_combine: the existing combiner reaches the same result on every example, and no measured gain
redundant_with_synthesized: other selected rules reach the same result on every example, and no measured gain
not_fired: does not apply to its own example, and no measured gain
unobserved: its guard never passes on the target corpus (it was learned from seed inputs only), and no measured gain
never_fires: applicable in the corpus but never fired when the corpus was compiled with every candidate (another rule gets there first)

no_measured_gain: inside the selected set it removes no instruction from the final code and its guard queries known bits (cost without measured benefit); rules without a known-bits guard are kept, but not a rule that moves an operation to a wider type
